studies.title: Chronic Kidney Disease Risk Posed by 1-Ethoxy-2,3-difluoro-4-(trans-4-propylcyclohexyl) Benzene (EDPrB): An AOP of mTOR-Mediated Autophagy Dysregulation.
studies.finding: In mice, the environmental pollutant EDPrB accumulates in the kidney and causes CKD via mTOR hyperactivation, leading to autophagy dysregulation, inflammation and fibrosis; rapamycin rescue identified mTOR as the molecular initiating event, with corroborating data in HK-2 human kidney cells.

studies.title: mTOR signalling and cellular metabolism are mutual determinants in cancer
studies.finding: Review of mTOR and cellular metabolism as mutual determinants in cancer.

studies.title: Efficacy of everolimus in advanced renal cell carcinoma: a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled phase III trial
studies.finding: Everolimus extended median progression-free survival from 1.9 to 4.0 months versus placebo in metastatic renal cell carcinoma.

studies.title: ER-Lysosome Cholesterol Exchange Regulates Lysosomal Motility Through mTOR-Dependent LAMTOR1 Phosphorylation
studies.finding: Identifies a new layer of control over mTORC1's lysosomal machinery: cholesterol exchange between the ER and lysosome regulates lysosome movement via mTOR-dependent phosphorylation of LAMTOR1, a core component of the Ragulator complex that anchors the Rag GTPases already in this Atlas.

studies.title: A substrate-specific mTORC1 pathway underlies Birt-Hogg-Dubé syndrome.
studies.finding: A substrate-specific mTORC1-TFEB pathway (RagC/D-dependent) drives Birt-Hogg-Dube kidney disease.

studies.title: TFEB links autophagy to lysosomal biogenesis
studies.finding: Showed that TFEB drives a coordinated autophagy and lysosomal gene programme during starvation. In this paper TFEB was regulated by ERK2 phosphorylation; its control by mTORC1 at the lysosome was established in later work (SET2012).

studies.title: A gene network regulating lysosomal biogenesis and function
studies.finding: The authors found that most lysosomal genes show coordinated expression and share a promoter motif (later called the CLEAR element) that is bound and regulated by the transcription factor TFEB. Under conditions of abnormal lysosomal storage, TFEB moved from the cytoplasm to the nucleus and switched on its target genes. studies.title: SLC38A9 is a component of the lysosomal amino acid sensing machinery that controls mTORC1
studies.finding: SLC38A9 is a component of the lysosomal amino-acid sensing machinery controlling mTORC1.

studies.title: mTOR inhibition augments antitumor immune effector response by reprogramming the TP53-mutant, immune-cold HNSCC tumor microenvironment
studies.finding: In syngeneic TP53-mutant HNSCC mouse models, the mTOR inhibitor everolimus reprogrammed the immune-cold tumor microenvironment: it increased CD8+ T cell and dendritic cell infiltration, reduced Tregs and HIF-1α/VEGFA-driven MDSC recruitment, boosted TNF-α/CXCL10 chemokine signaling, and reduced PD-1/PD-L1 expression — restoring T-cell cytotoxic competence and suppressing tumor growth.

studies.title: mTOR inhibits autophagy by controlling ULK1 ubiquitylation, self-association and function through AMBRA1 and TRAF6
studies.finding: mTOR restrains autophagy by controlling ULK1 ubiquitylation and stability via AMBRA1/TRAF6.

studies.title: Collagen I promotes cancer cell survival via amino acid import and mTORC1/S6 activation
studies.finding: Collagen I drives alpha2beta1 integrin-dependent mTORC1/S6 activation and membrane localization of the LAT1-4F2hc amino acid transporter, sustaining essential amino acid supply and cancer cell survival in nutrient-poor, collagen-rich tumor stroma; LAT1-4F2hc is upregulated in basal-like breast/pancreatic tumors and correlates with poor prognosis.

studies.title: Everolimus Aging Study (EVERLAST): Clinical Evaluation of mTORC1 Inhibition for Geroprotection
studies.finding: Phase 2 trial (NCT05835999, EVERLAST) testing this Atlas's open dosing hypothesis directly: whether daily low-dose (0.5 mg/day) or weekly (5 mg/week) everolimus for 24 weeks can improve physiological and molecular hallmarks of aging in insulin-resistant or prediabetic adults aged 55-80, without the metabolic penalty seen with continuous higher-dose rapalog use. studies.title: Enhanced sensitivity of PTEN-deficient tumors to inhibition of FRAP/mTOR
studies.finding: Tested whether tumour cells that have lost PTEN depend more on mTOR. The rapamycin analogue CCI-779 (temsirolimus) blocked growth of PTEN-null cells and tumours preferentially, and reversed the extra tumour growth caused by constitutively active Akt, placing mTOR downstream of Akt in tumour formation. studies.title: An inhibitor of mTOR reduces neoplasia and normalizes p70/S6 kinase activity in Pten+/- mice
studies.finding:
Transformed cells in Pten+/- mice showed raised phosphorylated Akt and active p70 S6 kinase together with faster proliferation. Treating the mice with an mTOR inhibitor reduced neoplastic proliferation, tumour size and S6 kinase activity without changing Akt status. The authors concluded that S6K and possibly other mTOR targets contribute to tumour development downstream of PTEN loss.

studies.title: Malonyl-CoA is a conserved endogenous ATP-competitive mTORC1 inhibitor
studies.finding: Malonyl-CoA, an intermediate of fatty-acid biosynthesis, binds the mTOR catalytic pocket directly and acts as a conserved ATP-competitive inhibitor of mTORC1; when fatty acid synthase is downregulated, rising malonyl-CoA feeds back to dampen mTORC1 activity, linking lipogenic capacity to overall biosynthetic output.

studies.finding: Raptor binds mTOR substrates via their TOS motifs, acting as the substrate-presenting scaffold of mTORC1.

studies.title: Circadian regulation of mTOR by the ubiquitin pathway in renal cell carcinoma
studies.finding: In mouse kidney tumours, active phosphorylated mTOR and total mTOR protein followed a 24-hour rhythm, set by the clock through the ubiquitin ligase Fbxw7. Giving everolimus when mTOR was high improved survival compared with other dosing times. Same drug, same dose - the clock time of dosing changed the outcome.

studies.title: Imaging dynamic mTORC1 pathway activity in vivo reveals marked shifts that support time-specific inhibitor therapy in AML
studies.finding: Fluorescent probes imaged in the bone marrow of live mice show mTORC1 activity in AML cells falls as the disease progresses but is high at the moment of maximal chemotherapy response, where it is induced rather than selected; inhibiting mTORC1 at that time improved killing of AML cells.

studies.title: Rheb is an essential regulator of S6K in controlling cell growth in Drosophila

studies.title: mTOR inhibition induces upstream receptor tyrosine kinase signaling and activates Akt
studies.finding: mTORC1 inhibition relieves feedback and activates upstream RTK-PI3K-Akt signalling. The Akt activation was demonstrated both in cancer cell lines and in patient tumours treated with RAD001 (everolimus), so this record carries a human pharmacodynamic component, not only in-vitro data.

studies.title: Amino acid deprivation inhibits TORC1 through a GTPase-activating protein complex for the Rag family GTPase Gtr1
studies.finding: The SEACIT complex is a GAP for the Rag/Gtr GTPases mediating amino-acid inhibition of TORC1.

studies.title: Sestrins inhibit mTORC1 kinase activation through the GATOR complex
studies.finding: Sestrins inhibit mTORC1 activation through the GATOR2 complex.

studies.title: Redefining the role of AMPK in autophagy and the energy stress response
studies.finding: In cultured cells, AMPK activation under glucose starvation or mitochondrial energy stress inhibited ULK1 and autophagy induction, the opposite of the classic activating reading. AMPK also protected the ULK1 machinery from caspase-mediated degradation.

studies.title: Transient APC/C inactivation by mTOR boosts glycolysis during cell cycle entry
studies.finding: After mitogen stimulation, mTOR quickly phosphorylates the APC/C adaptor CDH1, partly releasing it and briefly inactivating APC/C; the glycolytic enzyme PFKFB3 accumulates and glycolysis rises, until a delayed phosphatase restores APC/C. This incoherent feed-forward loop produces a pulse of glycolysis that cell cycle entry requires.

studies.finding: Folliculin (FLCN) gathers on lysosomes when amino acids are removed and binds RagA directly; FLCN is required for amino acids to recruit mTORC1 to lysosomes via the Rag GTPases.

studies.title: Biological limits of lifespan extension: evidence for a shift from pathway leverage to system-level buffering across species
studies.finding: mTOR/TOR pathway interventions achieve large lifespan extensions in simple organisms but face declining efficacy in mammals due to distributed multi-tissue buffering, redundancy, and pharmacokinetic complexity - proposing a unifying framework for the translational challenge of aging pathway targeting.

studies.title: Translational repression of 5' TOP mRNAs in chronically activated CD8+ T cells in vitro.
studies.finding: Ribosome profiling of exhausted human CD8+ T cells reveals marked repression of 5'TOP mRNAs despite elevated mTOR activity, uncovering a layer of translational control that overrides or bypasses mTOR in T cell exhaustion.

studies.title: Absence of S6K1 protects against age- and diet-induced obesity while enhancing insulin sensitivity
studies.finding: S6K1 deletion protects mice from age- and diet-induced obesity and enhances insulin sensitivity.

studies.title: Adipose-specific knockout of raptor results in lean mice with enhanced mitochondrial respiration
studies.finding: Adipose raptor knockout yields lean, metabolically protected mice, revealing mTORC1's role in fat metabolism.

studies.title: SREBP activity is regulated by mTORC1 and contributes to Akt-dependent cell growth
studies.finding: mTORC1 activates SREBP to drive lipogenesis supporting Akt-dependent cell growth.

studies.title: Role of AMP-activated protein kinase in mechanism of metformin action

studies.finding: 4 weeks of high-dose resveratrol had no effect on insulin sensitivity, blood pressure, or body composition - directly contradicting the promising rodent data that drove the original hype.

studies.finding: Rapamycin induces dephosphorylation/inactivation of the 70 kDa S6 kinase, defining an early readout of TOR signalling.

studies.title: Overexpression of Atg5 in mice activates autophagy and extends lifespan
studies.finding: Mice engineered with extra copies of the autophagy gene Atg5 lived 17% longer and were leaner and more insulin-sensitive.

studies.finding: mTOR sets how fast and how strongly the circadian clock ticks. Inhibiting mTOR lengthened the clock period and flattened its amplitude; activating it shortened the period and raised the amplitude, in cells, in ex vivo brain (SCN) and liver clocks, and in mTOR heterozygous mice, whose locomotor rhythm ran longer. studies.title: An SLC7A5-dependent nutrient-sensing circuit overcomes cisplatin tolerance via mTOR-autophagy signaling.
studies.finding: A genome-wide CRISPR screen found that mTOR inhibition promotes cisplatin tolerance by activating cytoprotective autophagy — the opposite of the canonical view. SLC7A5 integrates this mTOR-autophagy axis, and leucine supplementation resensitises SLC7A5-expressing tumour cells to cisplatin.

studies.title: Tankyrase-2 regulates adipocyte differentiation through AMPK/mTOR signaling.
studies.finding: Deleting TNKS1 or TNKS2 slows adipocyte differentiation, with inhibited autophagy, AMPK activation and suppressed mTORC1; the TNKS2-knockout defect is rescued by NV-5138 or by LKB1 inhibition, and TNKS2 ADP-ribosylates LKB1 (cell line).

studies.title: Streptococcus anginosus-associated kynurenic acid drives PD-1 blockade resistance through an ITGA2-mTOR-CTSV axis in gastric cancer.
studies.finding: Tumor microbiota-derived kynurenic acid drives resistance to PD-1 blockade in gastric cancer through the ITGA2-mTOR-CTSV axis: kynurenic acid induces ITGA2 and inhibits an mTOR-dependent cascade, which sustains cathepsin V expression and suppresses CD8+ T cell cytotoxic function.

studies.title: TOR signaling and rapamycin influence longevity by regulating SKN-1/Nrf and DAF-16/FoxO
studies.finding: In C. elegans, genetic TORC1 inhibition extends lifespan through SKN-1/Nrf and DAF-16/FoxO, whereas rapamycin's lifespan effect requires SKN-1 but not DAF-16, apparently because it also hits TORC2.
